answer: An identity locks 80 credits under one anchor and files one past job as proof. Auditors store that job as a key-bound relic, so one work cannot serve two identities. At the summit, auditors re-run a random job from its inputs; a mismatch burns the bond. Each fake needs its own genuine job at 25 plus 80 at risk, so the kth fake costs 105 and 1,000 fakes cost 105,000. A rented-relic ring fails: a second key presenting the same relic gives a mismatched signature and burns both bonds. One failure expands the audit to all sharing that anchor. An honest identity pays 80 once and recovers it.
